    24	
    25	# Web Designer
    26	
    27	You design how users interact with Loom. Every screen, button, and piece of
    28	information is evaluated from the user's perspective: is it findable, is it
    29	clear, does it respect the user's time?
    30	
    31	## Primary Skill
    32	
    33	Your default lens is user experience. You evaluate interfaces by asking three
    34	questions in order:
    35	
    36	1. **Can the user find it?** (information architecture, navigation, visual hierarchy)
    37	2. **Can the user understand it?** (labels, layout, progressive disclosure)
    38	3. **Can the user complete the task?** (interaction flow, error recovery, feedback)
    39	
    40	### Design workflow
    41	
    42	1. **Clarify the goal** — what user task does this interface serve? Write it as a single sentence.
    43	2. **Map the flow** — sketch the steps from entry to completion. Identify decision points and error states.
    44	3. **Design the layout** — establish visual hierarchy. Primary action prominent, secondary actions accessible but not competing.
    45	4. **Validate accessibility** — check color contrast (WCAG AA minimum), touch targets (44px minimum), keyboard flow, screen reader order.
    46	5. **Review** — walk through the flow as three user types: first-time, returning, power user.
    47	
    48	### Example: designing a bead status filter
    49	
    50	```
    51	Goal: Let users filter the bead list by status (open, in-progress, closed).
    52	
    53	Flow:
    54	  1. User sees bead list (default: all statuses).
    55	  2. User clicks filter control -> dropdown appears with status options.
    56	  3. User selects one or more statuses -> list updates immediately.
    57	  4. Active filters shown as removable chips above the list.
    58	
    59	Layout decisions:
    60	  - Filter control placed top-left, aligned with list header (scan line).
    61	  - Chips use distinct background color with "x" dismiss button (44px target).
    62	  - Empty state: "No beads match this filter" with clear-all action.
    63	
    64	Accessibility:
    65	  - Filter dropdown: aria-haspopup="listbox", arrow key navigation.
    66	  - Chips: role="status" with aria-label "Remove filter: open".
    67	  - Live region announces "Showing 12 beads" on filter change.
    68	```
    69	
    70	## Org Position
    71	
    72	- **Reports to:** Product Manager
    73	- **Direct reports:** None
    74	
    75	## Available Skills
    76	
    77	You are not limited to design. Use other skills when the situation demands it:
    78	
    79	- **Front-end code** — implement your designs directly in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript when that is faster than handing off.
    80	- **Documentation** — update UI screenshots and usage guides when designs change.
    81	- **Backend adjustments** — when a design change requires a small backend tweak (e.g., adding a display field to an API response), make it yourself.
    82	
    83	**When to do it yourself vs delegate:**
    84	- **Do it yourself:** The implementation is straightforward CSS/HTML and you can ship it faster than writing a handoff spec.
    85	- **Delegate:** The change requires complex state management, database changes, or performance-critical code.
    86	- **Call a meeting:** The design affects multiple product areas or changes established interaction patterns.
    87	
    88	## Model Selection
    89	
    90	- **Design decisions** (UX flow, information architecture, interaction patterns): strongest model — nuanced reasoning required
    91	- **CSS/layout implementation** (translating approved designs to code): mid-tier model
    92	- **Quick mockups** (rough wireframes, placeholder layouts): lightweight model

1	# ClipCast — One video is worth a thousand words
     2

     4	ClipCast is a free screen recorder and async video messaging platform that helps teams communicate faster with AI-powered video creation, editing, and sharing. Built for professionals, remote teams, and enterprises seeking modern async communication tools.

    11	CTA: "Get ClipCast for free" | "Install Chrome Extension"

    18	Label: New!

ClipCast automatically captures the technical details devs need (device/browser/OS, console errors, and network activity) to pinpoint the problem fast and move work forward.
    21	CTA: "Learn more"

    24	Title: The easiest screen recorder you'll ever use
    25	Subtitle: Record in a few clicks. Share anywhere. Collaborate better.
    26	Subsection Title: Lightning fast screen recording
    27	Description: Easily record your screen and camera. Record on any device using ClipCast's Chrome extension, desktop app, or mobile app.

    31	Title: So much more than a screen recorder
    32	- **Edit your videos like a pro** — ClipCast's intuitive editor lets you trim, stitch clips, add eye-catching backgrounds, and even enhance your message with text, arrows, and box overlays. The result? Engaging videos you can deliver fast.
    33	- **Share or embed video anywhere you work** — From Google Workspace to Slack, ClipCast videos seamlessly integrate with hundreds of tools you use every day.
    34	- **Engage and connect with video** — Easily collaborate by adding emojis, comments, tasks and CTAs to your video message. Empower remote teams to communicate better across timezones using transcripts and captions in 50+ languages.
    35	
    36	## Feature: Security
    37	Title: Keep your content safe
    38	Description: Enterprise-grade security to keep your data and your customer's data private and secure. We offer SSO, SCIM as well as custom data retention policies and privacy settings.
    39	CTA: "Learn more"

    42	- GDPR, CCPA, and SOC 2 Type 2 compliant
    43	- Built on the AWS-backbone with secure and reliable infrastructure
    44	- Equipped with advanced admin controls to protect sensitive information internally
    45	- Secured with encrypted data and industry-standard security frameworks

    49	- **Sales** — Personalize your pitch with video outreach to close more deals.
    50	- **Engineering** — Add visual context to your code to accelerate your sprints.
    51	- **Customer support** — Troubleshoot over video to reach resolutions faster.
    52	- **Design** — Share ideas and provide feedback over video to enhance designs.
    53	CTA: "See all use cases"

    56	Title: Powerful features for easy, custom recordings
    57	- Screen and camera recording
    58	- Easy sharing and embedding
    59	- Trim and stitch video clips
    60	- Download and upload
    61	- Transcriptions and closed captions
    62	- Video privacy controls
    63	- Custom background
    64	- Video and viewer insights
    65	CTA: "See all features"

    67	## Enterprise Impact Stats
    68	- **50%** fewer meetings across organizations
    69	- **18%** increase in traffic on webpages with ClipCast videos
    70	- **19%** boost in reply rates across sales outreach
    71	
    72	## Enterprise Async Video Benefits
    73	Title: Communicate faster with async video
    74	- **Save time** — Teams can communicate more efficiently without typing long emails, scheduling meetings, or trying to work across time zones.
    75	- **Communicate clearly** — Async video captures context, tone, and personality in detail. Distributed teams can preserve the true meaning of their message.
    76	- **Deepen culture** — Make it effortless for anyone in your organization to share ideas, introduce themselves, and build community with fellow teammates using async video.
    77	
    78	## Enterprise Community & Visibility
    79	Title: Drive community and visibility at scale
    80	- **Scale knowledge with video** — Connect pockets of institutional knowledge by making video messages searchable and discoverable.
    81	- **Create a culture of sharing** — Video messaging encourages your team to share early and often so projects are visible and driven to completion quicker.
    82	- **Build community at scale** — Magnify people's voices so the whole company can feel connected and heard beyond the boundaries of their team.

steps.message:
All 5 pages have been built and validated. Here's a summary of what was delivered:

### Output Files (`/app/output/`)

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `index.html` | Home page with 15 sections: hero, logo bar, AI bug reports, screen recorder, video editor, integrations, engagement, security, use cases, features grid, blog teasers, enterprise CTA, testimonials, CTA banner, footer |
| `enterprise.html` | Enterprise page with hero, logo bar, async video benefits, community & visibility, testimonial quote, security grid, use cases, stats (50%/18%/19%), integrations, pricing plans, testimonials carousel, CTA banner |
| `pricing.html` | Pricing page with billing toggle (monthly/annual + "Save up to 17%" badge), team size slider, 4 plan cards, AI features grid, full comparison table, FAQ accordion |
| `login.html` | Login page with social auth (Google, Slack, Apple, Outlook, SSO), email input, testimonial sidebar |
| `signup.html` | Signup page with Google auth, email input, testimonial sidebar, login link |
| `css/styles.css` | Complete design system with responsive breakpoints |
| `js/main.js` | Cookie banner/modal, FAQ accordion, pricing toggle, team slider |

### Key Interactions Implemented
- **Cookie consent** on home page: accept/reject/manage preferences with category toggles modal
- **Pricing toggle**: switches between monthly ($18/$24) and annual ($15/$20) pricing
- **Team size slider**: 1–100 people with visual plan recommendation highlight
- **FAQ accordion**: expand/collapse answers
- **Navigation**: consistent shared nav across all pages with correct inter-page links
- **All CTAs** route to signup or login as specified
